summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted due to a high amikacin trough level of 9.0 and inability to manage his complex IV antibiotic regimen at home. He has a history of liver transplant and recent pseudomonas bacteremia and urinary tract infection requiring prolonged antibiotic therapy. During the 3-day stay, amikacin was held initially, then restarted after a safe trough level was confirmed. Meropenem was continued with extended infusions. The patient's kidney function remained stable despite baseline acute kidney issues, and hyperkalemia was monitored without intervention. Diarrhea was evaluated and found not to be due to C. diff. Malnutrition was noted with low albumin, and nutritional support was recommended. Given his self-care limitations, discharge was arranged to an extended care facility to complete antibiotic treatment. Follow-up includes post-treatment blood and urine cultures and ongoing monitoring through the transplant clinic.
